Features

Make heavy CAD models light. Free, private, on your own machine.

Before and after

Drag the line. Same axle, far fewer triangles.

On the left is the front axle as it came, 250,075 triangles. On the right is what the app’s own simplifier makes of it. Pick how far to go and drag the line to compare.

Model: Mercedes-Benz Arocs 8×8 front axle. Trademarks belong to their owners; not affiliated. The right side is a real run of the simplifier the app’s Decimate uses; the numbers are counted, not typed.

Fasteners

Find every bolt. Take it out.

This engine is 1,295 parts, and 376 of them are bolts, nuts and washers. Find them, take them out, and watch what that does to the triangle count. Drag to turn the model.

Model: a Scania V8 engine, a light copy made for this page. Trademarks belong to their owners; not affiliated. Here the fasteners are picked out by part name; the app finds them by their shape, in one click.

Mesh clean-up

The tools this app is for.

Bolt holes nobody will see. Screws sealed inside housings. Parts drawn twice. Found by shape, gone in one click, back with one undo.

Smaller files

5 MB in. 1 MB out.

Same model, same shape, a fraction of the file. Send it, load it, share it.

Gearbox, Meshopt

79% smaller file size 4.95 MB → 1.03 MB

Gearbox, file size

4.95 MBPlain GLB
1.03 MB−79%Meshopt
0.59 MB−88%Draco
Meshopt
Small and quick to open. About a fifth of the size, built for the web.
Draco
The smallest file. About an eighth of the size, for when every kilobyte counts.
Faster to draw
Same file size, smoother on screen. Opens in any viewer.

Measured on the Khronos sample models (Gearbox, Reciprocating Saw, Two-Cylinder Engine) with glTF Transform 4.1: Meshopt at high, Draco at its defaults. 1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes. Very light meshes can come out larger with Draco.

Import

Open and convert

  • Reads the whole assemblyColours, names and the whole part tree come through.
  • Finds repeatsSame shape, any angle: stored once, drawn many times.
  • Rebuilds the surfacesSet the detail in millimetres, or as a share of the model.
  • You set the tessellationBig parts fine, screws light. You choose the detail by part size.
  • Smooth from the CAD surfacesFillets blend, cylinders have no seam, sharp edges stay sharp.
  • CompressesMeshopt turns your GLBs into a fraction of the size.

Make it light

Clean up and optimise

  • Smart optimisev1Scans the model first and lists what it found, with Highlight and Isolate for each. Then every clean-up in one press. One undo.
  • Fastenersv6Every bolt, screw, nut and washer, found by shape.
  • Select hidden partsv2The parts nobody can see, found in one click.
  • Remove hidden facesv1Faces that never show, gone: inside housings, where parts meet.
  • Quick decimate (B)v4Slide down a column of levels and watch the part change.
  • Fit to budgetv4Name a triangle count. The heaviest meshes go first.

Make it right

Repair and tidy

  • Remove holesv15Bolt holes, slots and pockets closed, with no ring of points left behind.
  • Remove floating piecesv2Plugs, shavings and stray dots, gone.
  • Repair meshv2Doubled points, empty triangles, flipped faces: fixed.
  • Splitv6One fused lump, back to the solids it was, or a mesh with several materials, one part for each.
  • Stacked copiesv1Parts drawn twice in the same place, removed. Only true copies go.
  • Align to floorA model that arrived on its side, stood up, with a preview first.

Go inside

Edit mesh

  • Points, edges, polygonsPick the pieces of a mesh. Keys 1 to 4 switch mode.
  • Click, Box, BrushThree ways to pick. Double-click takes the whole loop.
  • Move what you pickedMove, turn and scale pieces with the gizmo. One undo.
  • Dissolvev4Points out, surface closed, no hole.
  • Weld and Fillv1Join points. Close a hole from its rim.
  • Planarize and Straightenv1Flat polygons. Straight lines of edges.

Big assemblies

Find and organise

  • Built for big assembliesTen thousand rows, still smooth.
  • Search and filtersFind parts by name, with the small ones tinted.
  • Search (Shift + C)Commands, settings, parts, library: one box. Typos and initials still find it.
  • Batch rename (F2)Templates, regex, live preview, presets.
  • Select by ruleName, material, size, triangles: pick by rule, with a live count.
  • Typo-proof part searchWords in any order, quotes, or, minus, >5000 triangles. A typo still finds it.

Make new parts

Build and arrange

  • A Draw tool (L)Pen, rectangle, circle, arc, polygon, freehand: on any plane or on a part’s face.
  • Align partsAlign or spread parts and whole groups along X, Y and Z, with a gap if you want one. One undo.
  • Sweepv2Carry a profile along a path. Scale, twist, closed ends. The result is a normal part.
  • A library of 112 partsBolts, nuts, pipe fittings, bearings, brackets, gears, a servo. Set the size, drag it in.
  • Exploded viewOne slider pulls it apart, along the axes you choose.
  • Dynamic place (D)Drag a part over a surface: it rests on it and turns to face it.

Send it on

Export and deliver

  • GLB and glTFDraco or Meshopt compression. Textures embedded if you want.
  • FBX, USDZ, OBJ, STL, PLYThe common 3D and AR formats, with mm, cm, m and inch presets.
  • Check against where it’s goingTest the scene against web, Shopify, AR Quick Look or phone-app limits.
  • Parts listA CSV bill of materials: every part and its size.
  • Lighter, or just faster to drawMeshopt cuts a GLB to about a quarter. Or keep the size and draw faster.

Notes

Review together

  • Notes on the modelPress N, click a spot, write. A numbered pin stays on the part, with a picture of the view it was written from.
  • Replies, edits and resolveAnyone can answer, edit or resolve. An edit keeps what it replaced; a delete leaves who deleted it.
  • Every change has a nameType your name once. Every note, comment and edit shows who and when, and each note has a history.
  • Notes in the scene fileSaved with the scene and opened with it. Export never writes notes, so a team comment cannot reach a customer.
  • Bring in another copy’s notesTwo people each worked on a copy? Bring in the other file and the notes are joined. Nobody’s words are lost.
  • A report anyone can openThe notes as one HTML page with pictures, who said what and the history. No app needed.

The app

Make it yours

  • Keyboard remapperThe shortcuts window is a keyboard: lit keys carry their command, and holding Ctrl, Shift or Alt shows what those do. Click a shortcut, press new keys, and a key that is taken warns you first. Keep your set in a profile, one per person.
  • A look of your ownAccent colour, tones, font, text size, corners and density.
  • Numbers you dragDrag any number sideways to change it, or click to type. Right-click to reset, step, double or halve it.
  • Cards over the modelTools open as cards you can move. Enter runs, Esc closes.
  • Scene tabsEach tab is its own scene. Opening a file never replaces your work. Copy parts from one tab, or one window, into another.
  • Floating Materials and LibraryPop either out as a window, move it, resize it. Both open side by side.

Ask for it

Work with Claude

  • Just askSay “find the bolts and hide them” or “get this under 5 MB”. Claude does it with the app’s 78 tools.
  • You decideIt asks before it changes anything. Deleting always asks. Every change is one undo.
  • Try it firstSixteen steps can be tried first: done, shown, taken back.
  • One request, a whole jobUnder 5 MB, or ready for web, Shopify, AR or phone, with a before and after picture.
  • A whole folderEvery model in a folder: opened, optimised, exported, closed. Stop it any time.
  • Pictures for a clientClean renders up to 8192 px, several angles, a plain or transparent background, plus a turntable film.
